published_source: Authors' Stata log (Table6.log, esttab output re-run by the authors on the shipped data); no article text or PDF in the project.
data_provenance: real (anonymized: README says identifiers and some variables were modified to protect proprietary information while preserving consistency; not synthetic; the shipped data reproduce the authors' logs exactly)
replication_status: exact (fixest reproduces the authors' log coefficient, SE and N; published article not available to compare)
notes: CONTROLS ANALYSIS (PROTOCOL 5c). Authors: reghdfe distance_from_home_46 did beauty_num culture_num transport_num cafe_num housing_num mart_num medical_num, absorb(date1 newid) vce(cluster newid) on Data/Table6_dataset.dta. did = subscribe x post; post switches on at the user's own subscription date (absorbing, no switch-offs); 1:1 matched sample of subscribers and never-subscribers (matching on Jan-Jul 2019 user means; PROTOCOL 5b: matched sample = sample restriction). Only violation: seven daily category transaction counts as time-varying controls, entered linearly. Unit = user (newid), time = day (date_num = days since 1970-01-01), user and date FE, no weights, clustered by user. Selected user-day sample shipped by the authors (only user-days where the outcome family is defined; unbalanced). The user ids in this file are coded differently from Table1_dateset.dta (onset dates there do not match), and the file has no subscription-date column, so treat_var = did is used: run_spec dates onset at the first observed treated day, which can be later than the true subscription day; TWFE and BJS are unaffected, CSA cohort timing would be. DEVIATIONS: none for TWFE (singletons kept by run_spec; reghdfe drops them, which leaves the coefficient unchanged). CSA on the daily panel is expected to hit the size guard (up to 137 daily cohorts x 396 days).
